title: Acabar de + infinitivo: algo que acaba de suceder

sections.content: Acabar de + infinitive marks an action as having just finished, right before the moment being described -- useful here for capturing how suddenly the 1920s boom turned into panic, with investors who had barely finished enjoying a decade of growth. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los inversores, que apenas acababan de disfrutar de casi una década de crecimiento aparentemente imparable, entraron en pánico.
items.english: Investors, who had barely just finished enjoying almost a decade of seemingly unstoppable growth, panicked.

items.spanish: Millones de personas que acababan de perder buena parte de sus ahorros se lanzaron a retirar dinero de los bancos.
items.english: Millions of people who had just lost much of their savings rushed to withdraw money from the banks.

items.spanish: Los bancos estadounidenses apenas acababan de vivir una década prestando generosamente a gobiernos y empresas de todo el mundo.
items.english: American banks had barely just finished a decade of generously lending to governments and companies around the world.

items.spanish: El resultado fue una crisis que, aunque había comenzado en Nueva York, no tardaría en sentirse en cualquier rincón del planeta.
items.english: The result was a crisis that, although it had begun in New York, would soon be felt in practically every corner of the planet.

sections.content: Acababan de + infinitive is conjugated in the imperfect here because the whole scene is set in the past -- for a present-tense equivalent ("has just happened"), you'd instead say acaba de + infinitive.
